title: Probe Selection Criteria
description: Essential Criteria: The response must include the de Broglie wavelength condition for selecting probes, specifically that the wavelength must be less than or equal to the size of the nucleus.

title: Electron Advantages
description: Important Criteria: The advantages of using electrons as probes should be clearly stated, including their interaction characteristics and ease of analysis.

title: Electron Disadvantages
description: Important Criteria: The disadvantages of using electrons, particularly the requirement for high energy beams, must be discussed.

title: Proton Advantages
description: Important Criteria: The advantages of using protons, such as the availability of high flux beams, should be mentioned.

title: Proton Disadvantages
description: Important Criteria: The response must address the complexity of analyzing proton-nucleus interactions due to multiple types of interactions.

title: Neutron Advantages
description: Important Criteria: The advantages of neutrons as probes, particularly their lack of charge, should be included.

title: Neutron Disadvantages
description: Important Criteria: The difficulties in generating and detecting neutron beams must be discussed.

title: Photon Opinion
description: Optional Criteria: The opinion on using photons should reflect their hadron-like character and the complications it introduces.

title: Common Errors
description: Pitfall Criteria: The response should avoid common errors such as misrepresenting the conditions for probe selection or failing to mention the complexities of proton interactions.
